fit.verdict: The best-matched of the four roles, and it keeps getting stronger as the real body of work surfaces. Leroy is a practicing tax preparer who builds accounting software: Well (a PUBLISHED Chrome Web Store product that automates supplier-invoice retrieval into QuickBooks/Xero — i.e. Mercury's literal problem statement), ReconcileIQ (an account-reconciliation app with real clients incl. a Form 990 nonprofit), and TaxesByRoss (the platform behind his own tax practice). Plus TOBA (a live 501(c)(3) platform build with a monthly board-member cadence, full-board product presentations, a written SOP + licensing + continuity-agreement handoff, and three documented board objections he resolved — data sovereignty, duplication, and cost), InsureBridge, and Titan Couriers. All five are built as structured case studies on the Paintbrush /use-cases page — each in its own visual language, with real logos and brand colors and a geometrically-accurate device frame — plus a standalone 1-page decision record for the TOBA consolidation. The remaining gap is narrow: the case-study screens are still coded skeletons rather than real product screenshots, and collaboration has been design + stakeholders rather than design + PM + eng + research inside a product org.

criteria.name: 6+ yrs leading complex, end-to-end product design initiatives
criteria.note: 10+ yrs, 'Product Designer & Partner', and a deep bench of shipped products — Well (published), ReconcileIQ, TaxesByRoss, TOBA (multi-surface, board stakeholders), InsureBridge, Titan. No engineering partner or formal research is what keeps it at 8, not 9.

criteria.name: Thinks in systems & workflows, not screens
criteria.note: Data-driven architecture, Style Registry governance, the TOBA permissions model, Well's self-healing workflow blueprints and multi-format export system.

criteria.name: Learns new domains obsessively until can challenge experts
criteria.note: He doesn't learn accounting — he has run a private tax practice since 2015 (150+ clients), prepares Form 990 filings on contract for Trydent Advisors (Tallahassee), and built both his practice software (TaxesByRoss) and a published invoice-automation product (Well). Domain operator, not learner.

criteria.name: Turning highly complex workflows into simple experiences
criteria.note: Well's whole shipped pitch is 'days of clicking and chasing invoices -> one click'. Plus ReconcileIQ, courier dispatch, checkout, admin intake.

criteria.name: Balances automation with transparency, trust, user control
criteria.note: 'Human-approved, never auto-sends' agents; TOBA audit trail; Well's invoice-data validation, an AI receipt-fraud detector, and 'no passwords stored, GDPR/CCPA'.

criteria.name: Product judgment, clear communication, high ownership
criteria.note: Now well-evidenced across all three sub-signals in the TOBA case study. JUDGMENT: redirected TOBA from 'random information' to systematic feature-by-feature building; scoped the committee consolidation and pitched it to the full board. COMMUNICATION: monthly cadence with the committee-lead board member, full-board product presentations, a written handoff package to the org's marketing lead (SOP intro, Licensing & Continuity Plan, Deploy & Dev SOP, formal Continuity Agreement). ALIGNMENT UNDER DISAGREEMENT: three documented board objections resolved — (1) Finance chair, data sovereignty -> gave TOBA its own AWS account, datasets, and backend (the objection changed the architecture); (2) Youth Development chair, duplication with an in-progress internal effort -> no forced switch, adoption by comparison once the workspace was real; (3) Leadership Institute chair, infrastructure cost -> none, pro bono, cost scope fixed in the Continuity Agreement. OWNERSHIP: ships the platform AND wrote the continuity/licensing terms so the org is never stranded. All of this is now packaged — the TOBA case study 'working with the board' section plus a standalone 1-page decision record (decision-record-toba-consolidation.md). Held at 9, not 10: still a volunteer board rather than a product-company PM/eng/research pod, and no formal user research.

criteria.name: Uses AI to accelerate exploration without compromising craft
criteria.note: Provider routing, fine-tuning, explicit 'where AI does not belong' rules — and Well is an AI-native accounting product (extractor, fraud detector, receipt generator).

criteria.name: Polished UI craft
criteria.note: Well, ReconcileIQ, TaxesByRoss, InsureBridge, TOBA are all real product UI, and each now has a structured case study on /use-cases in its own visual language with real logos and brand colors — up from folder names / a Chrome listing / one-line cards. Still short of 8-9 until real product screenshots replace the coded skeleton screens. Kraken is a branding project, not product UI.
